question.problem: A cinema hall can hold $120$ people. The price of each ticket is $$10.$ The cost of maintaining the cinema is made up of a fixed cost of $$400$ plus a cost of $$0.25$ per person. How many tickets should the cinema sell to maximize its profit?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we apply the candidates test.

First, note that for selling $x$ tickets, the cinema has a revenue (in dollars) of 

$$
R(x)=10\cdot x=10x
$$

and a cost (in dollars) of 

$$
C(x)={{400}_{⏟}}_{\text{fixed cost}}\,\,+{{0.25x.}_{⏟}}_{\text{variable cost}}
$$

Therefore, the profit function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x) & =R(x)-C(x) \\  & =10x-(400+0.25x) \\  & =9.75x-400.\end{aligned}
$$

We note that the permitted domain is $0\le x\le 120.$ Therefore, $x=0$ and $x=120$ are candidates for the global maxima of $P(x).$

We need to find the critical points of $P(x)$ for $0<x<120.$ Taking the derivative, we get

$$
{P}^{′}(x)=9.75.
$$

We can see that the equation ${P}^{′}(x)=0$ has no solutions.

Our candidates are $x=0$ and $x=120.$ Computing $P(x)$ at each of these values, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0) & =9.75(0)-400=-400 \\ P(120) & =9.75(120)-400=770\text{ }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the cinema will have a maximum profit level when it sells $120$ tickets.
